summary: Check whether a binary tree is height-balanced (every node's subtree heights differ by at most 1).
mainInsight: Compute heights bottom-up and check the balance condition at every node in the same traversal; returning a sentinel (-1) for 'unbalanced' lets you stop early and keeps the whole check at O(n).

approaches.name: Top-down height checks
approaches.summary: At every node compute both heights recursively.

approaches.name: Bottom-up single pass
approaches.summary: dfs returns the height and records/flags imbalance.

personalSolution.approach: Bottom-up single pass with a flag
personalSolution.notes: Optimal; a -1 sentinel allows early termination.

promptVariants: Which traversal order checks balance in O(n)?
How do you avoid recomputing heights?
options: Postorder: return the height and check balance on the way back up
Preorder traversal that calls a separate height helper at every node
Breadth-first traversal that compares the sizes of consecutive levels
Inorder traversal that checks the sorted order of the visited node values
cards.answer: Postorder: return the height and check balance on the way back up
cards.explanation: Children heights are available when the parent is processed, so each node's check is O(1).

incorrectOptionExplanations.Preorder traversal that calls a separate: That is the O(n^2) top-down approach.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Breadth-first traversal that compares th: Level order does not give subtree heights directly.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Inorder traversal that checks the sorted: Does not provide subtree heights at the node.

promptVariants: Why can you compute balance and height in the same recursion?
What does each call return and check?
cards.answer: A node is balanced iff both subtrees are balanced and their heights differ by at most 1. The recursion returns the height; at each node it compares the two child heights (the balance check) and returns max + 1 for the parent - one visit per node.
cards.explanation: A sentinel -1 can also propagate 'unbalanced' to stop early.

promptVariants: Time complexity of the bottom-up solution: ___
Complete the statement: Time complexity of the bottom-up solution: ___
Complete the statement: Recursion stack space (h = height): ___
cards.explanation: Depth of the recursion equals the tree height.

promptVariants: Why does your dfs keep running after setting `self.ans = False`, and how would a sentinel value prune it?
What is the role of `max(left, right) + 1`?
cards.answer: The flag does not stop the traversal, so the rest of the tree is still visited (still O(n) overall). Returning -1 as an 'unbalanced' sentinel and short-circuiting (`if left == -1: return -1`) prunes the remaining work. `max(left, right) + 1` is the node's own height for its parent.
cards.explanation: Both are O(n) in the worst case.

promptVariants: Is a tree where a node has a child with a deep chain below it but a missing sibling balanced?
What does the check look at?
options: Not necessarily: balance compares the two child heights at every node
Yes always, because a missing sibling can never make a node unbalanced
Only the root matters, so the subtrees below do not need to be checked
Only the leaves matter, because they carry all the height information
cards.answer: Not necessarily: balance compares the two child heights at every node
cards.explanation: A deep imbalance anywhere in the tree makes it unbalanced.
